findings.title: Live Bali cart currently refuses all order requests
findings.proof: live desktop/mobile browser and public GET
findings.impact: Customers can browse and add tea but the cart says the store cannot take orders; order-request submission is disabled. This blocks the intended inquiry-led journey before WhatsApp/email handoff.
findings.reproduction: Open https://teajia.com/shop, search Y562, open it, add 50g, open the order. Both widths showed the refusal. Public GET /api/s/teajia-bali returned can_be_paid:false. No customer details or orders were submitted.
findings.remedy: Owner: inspect the linked published Tea Master/payment destination and restore a published payment method if the store should accept orders. Do not remove the guard without a product decision.
findings.size: small operational check; exact missing configuration not available through public data
findings.dependencies: Public API does not distinguish missing recipient, unpublished profile, or missing payment method. Private admin configuration and intended closure state were not read. This is a verified operational state, not a proved recent regression.

findings.title: Admin product adapter collapses inherited freight and explicit zero values
findings.impact: NULL freight becomes a pinned free rate in admin; zero retail override becomes unset and zero stock threshold becomes 100. This immediately corrupts display/preview. Duplication then treats that zero as an explicit rate and can persist free freight in the new product. Existing server prices are not proved to have changed just by reading.
findings.reproduction: Feed useProducts a Worker row with shipping_rate_per_kg null, fixed_retail_price_usd 0, low_stock_threshold 0.
findings.remedy: Preserve null versus zero in the product adapter and add focused adapter cases.
findings.proof: actual React product hook + synthetic raw Worker row
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.

findings.title: Closed stores still serve public products and events
findings.impact: Private or suspended account catalog and event schedule remain available to unauthenticated callers who know the slug.

trace.detail: getAccountIdBySlug resolves any account slug, without public_enabled or status.
Public store profile requires public_enabled=1 and status=active.
Public products route uses the unrestricted slug resolver.
Public store events route uses the unrestricted slug resolver.

findings.reproduction: In local D1, seed an account with public_enabled=0 or status=suspended plus one public product and active event. GET /api/s/:slug returns 404; GET /api/s/:slug/products and /events both return 200 with content.
findings.smallestRemedy: Use getPublicAccountIdBySlug for both public child routes and add closure regression cases.
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.
findings.remedy: Use getPublicAccountIdBySlug for both public child routes and add closure regression cases.

findings.title: Private events are discoverable and reveal their address
findings.impact: Unauthenticated discovery includes events explicitly marked private, and the public detail route returns address_text and venue context.

trace.detail: Public event detail selects address_text and venue_guide.
Detail query filters only active event status.
Public event discovery ignores public_visibility, network_discovery, and account status.
Public RSVP creation checks only event status.
Store event discovery checks only event status and account ID.

findings.reproduction: In local D1, seed a future active event with public_visibility=private, network_discovery=0, and address_text. GET /api/events and /api/s/:slug/events include it; GET /api/events/:slug/public returns its address.
findings.smallestRemedy: Define and apply shared public event visibility predicates for discovery, direct detail, and RSVP, including an active/public host account gate.
findings.dependencies: Apply discovery versus direct-link policy deliberately: private must not be publicly discoverable; unlisted may permit direct links. Schema enum at worker/schema.sql:1572 and existing public-event predicate at worker/src/index.ts:10742 establish the distinction. No real private address was queried.
findings.remedy: Define and apply shared public event visibility predicates for discovery, direct detail, and RSVP, including an active/public host account gate.

findings.title: Shop collections disclose hidden products and closed stores
findings.impact: Public shop collection discovery can reveal active products whose is_public and shown_in_shop flags are both zero, including after the host store closes. The explicit publication explains initial inclusion but should not bypass subsequent public-discovery privacy flags. Whether a deliberately shared recipient link may retain hidden items is a separate policy question; the confirmed remediation target is /api/collections/shop.

trace.detail: Shop publication query has no host-account status/public gate.
Shop item query filters product status but not is_public or shown_in_shop.
Public collection link only checks publication and collection state.
Public link item projection filters only product status.

findings.reproduction: In local D1, seed private store, hidden active product (is_public=0, shown_in_shop=0), active collection and shop publication. GET /api/collections/shop and /api/public/c/:slug both return the product.
findings.smallestRemedy: Gate shop publications by open accounts and public, shown products; separately define whether recipient links may include private products.
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.
findings.remedy: Gate shop publications by open accounts and public, shown products; separately define whether recipient links may include private products.

findings.title: Stale order lines can overwrite a different pending order
findings.impact: A pending order can have its lines, prices, and stock reservations replaced by another order’s lines.
findings.reproduction: Open A and let its item request finish; close; open B in the same mounted EditOrderModal; reject B’s item request. It changes customer fields to B, retains A’s lines, clears fetching, and enables Save. Captured updateItems payload targets B with tea-a. This sequence needs no artificial race; a normal failed request is sufficient. The alternate late-A-response race is source-only.
findings.remedy: Clear lines before loading, ignore stale responses, and block save after load error.
findings.proof: actual React editor + mocked load failure and captured save payload
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.

findings.title: Save plus Share can create duplicate invoices after PDF/share failure
findings.impact: The invoice exists before PDF/share work. PDF failure leaves the creation form open with a failure toast; retry creates another invoice. The browser fixture hit a real PDF renderer hasOwnProperty error before navigator.share; cancellation was not browser-observed. The share promise is awaited inside the same try with no AbortError exception, so cancellation follows the same source path.
findings.reproduction: Click Save + Share in the supplied fixture twice. Observed: two mocked create calls, two renderer-failure toasts, no success/close. Independently submit the same synthetic Draft invoice twice to the real bundled Worker with in-memory D1: 201/201, distinct UUIDs and invoice numbers 00001/00002. No request-level idempotency key is consumed by this endpoint. The saving flag prevents simultaneous clicks only, and resets after the PDF error.
findings.remedy: Commit UI success after invoice create; retry sharing separately without another create.
findings.proof: actual React invoice modal/PDF failure + mocked creates; separate real Worker/in-memory D1 persistence proof
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.

findings.title: Unscoped persisted query keys can show prior-store financial and event data
findings.impact: PendingView retains account A’s customer/order data when account B’s refetch fails; its unscoped key survives account-switch invalidation. Sensitive disk-persistence exposure is established by the persister allow rules, not a separate observed logout incident. This is client-cache isolation, not a demonstrated server authorization bypass.
findings.reproduction: Load pending data in A, switch to B, delay or fail B request, open Pending tab.
findings.remedy: Key private queries by account and user, gate display by token scope, and exclude or purge sensitive persisted data.
findings.proof: actual PendingView + account switch/invalidation and injected fetch error
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.

findings.title: Article save can undo a successful publish
findings.reproduction: Edit an existing draft; let auto-save start; publish before save settles; allow publish to commit before the older update. The toast says published while the row ends as draft.
findings.proof: actual React editor; delayed mocked update commits after mocked publish
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.
findings.remedy: Serialize save and publish; flush pending content before publish and remove publication status from ordinary autosaves.
findings.impact: The editor displays Published and an Article published toast while a delayed pre-publish content update writes status=draft. The fixture reproduces request ordering and UI contradiction; ordinary Worker updates accept the status field, so that order can persist draft.

findings.title: Manual retry can double-receive a partial stock delivery
findings.reproduction: Receive 5g of an expected 20g; let write succeed and fail list refresh. The panel still shows 0 received/20 remaining and keeps the typed 5. Click Receive again: actual API creates a different key. Separate real Worker D1 probe accepts the two 5g intents and records 10g on hand. A repeated same-key request is correctly deduplicated; the problem is manual retry identity.
findings.impact: The second click uses a new key and can add another 5 to stock and the receipt ledger.
findings.smallestRemedy: Keep the intent's idempotency key until a confirmed result and block new receives on stale data pending reconciliation.
findings.proof: actual receipt panel + API retry-key capture; separate Worker/in-memory D1 stock proof
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.
findings.remedy: Keep the intent's idempotency key until a confirmed result and block new receives on stale data pending reconciliation.

findings.title: Incident intake trusts unverified tenant header
findings.impact: Any signed-in user can attribute an incident to another account; global signature dedupe can alter count, severity, and resolved state of an existing incident.

trace.detail: Handler uses requireAuth, which validates the session but does not authorize a tenant.
Handler passes raw X-Teajia-Account to upsertIncident.
Incident upsert merges by a global signature.

findings.reproduction: In local D1, user A belongs only to account A. POST /api/incidents with user A's JWT and X-Teajia-Account: account-b returned 201; the saved incident has account_id=account-b.
findings.smallestRemedy: Resolve account through live membership or store null for an untrusted global client report; review dedupe key tenancy.
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.
findings.remedy: Resolve account through live membership or store null for an untrusted global client report; review dedupe key tenancy.

findings.title: Find-a-table review badge always falls back to Verified
findings.impact: The review query is rejected and directory rows display an unsupported status; the count cannot represent distinct teas per store.

trace.detail: Review query expects an object with reviews.
Query sends visibility only.
Worker requires tea_key, product_id, or source_sample_id and returns 400 without one.
Caller reads reviewsData.reviews, but worker returns a raw array.
Count increments per row; the computed tea key is discarded.
Zero count becomes the Verified badge.

findings.runtimeProof: Parent browser pass observed GET /api/tea-reviews returning 400 on /find-a-table.

findings.title: Overlapping saves can create duplicate new articles
findings.reproduction: Type a new title, click Save as the auto-save timer fires, and keep both create responses pending. Both calls can submit with a null article ID.
findings.dependencies: No architecture change required; targeted regression coverage.
findings.remedy: Share one in-flight create promise, cancel a pending debounce before manual save, then update the returned ID.
